raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`radix_select_topk` in `fast_topk.cuh` treats "at most SMEM_INPUT_SIZE candidates in the threshold bin" as a correctness assumption. The coarse fp16 binning (~2 mantissa bits per bin) lets a concentrated row place far more candidates in one bin — 16K at L=30,938 and 34K at L=65,504 for QSA k=512 (reported in #36807 by @mochgolf). Overflowing candidates are dropped *together with* their fused histogram contributions, so the staged subset no longer represents the threshold-bin population and refinement silently selects from a truncated set: wrong top-k, run-to-run unstable, and no error is surfaced since the output still looks like exactly-k valid indices.

## Fix

Keep the fast path unchanged. Detect the overflow (`s_num_input[0] > SMEM_INPUT_SIZE`), then refine by rescanning the full row, filtering candidates by the coarse bin plus the refined radix digits selected in previous rounds (`s_prefix_bins`). No API change, no smem layout change, CUDA-graph / PDL safe.

The coarse-stage threshold selection itself stays exact: it runs on the full first-pass histogram *before* any staging truncation, and kTopK (512/2048) < SMEM_INPUT_SIZE (4096) makes a post-truncation boundary unreachable.

## Tests

- New regression `test_fast_topk_regression.py` (registered CUDA CI): concentrated rows at L=30,938 / 65,504 x k in {512, 2048} **fail on the unpatched source** (8 failed / 2 passed — wrong rows and unstable selections) and **pass with the fix** (10 passed); non-overflow N(0,1) controls unchanged.
  - **Update (09-28)**: the regression matrix has since been expanded to 33 cases — unpatched 8 failed / 25 passed, with the fix 33 passed / 0 failed (details in the 09-21 comment below).
- Existing `test_fast_topk.py`: 23 passed (no regression).
- End-to-end smoke on 8x A800 (SM80), TP8, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next: health 200, CUDA-graph capture (32 batch sizes) + replay OK, and a 42K-token long-context request answered correctly through the QSA `fast_topk` path (needle retrieval at the compressed attention layer).

## Performance

No measurable regression on non-overflow inputs (kernel micro-benchmark medians within run-to-run noise).

## Notes

- Complements #37786 (padded-extend-plan OOB); different root cause, different path.
- `fast_topk.cuh` now lives on main (imported by `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qsa/kernel.py` and `qsa_indexer.py`), so this patch applies directly to `main` with no stacking. Note that main's copy is still the unfixed one — the staging-overflow path this PR guards is live on main today.

<!-- pr-states:end -->

## Scope note

This fixes the JIT kernel (`python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/elementwise/fast_topk.cuh`) only. The AOT kernel (`python/sglang/kernels/aot/csrc/elementwise/topk.cu`) shares the same staging-overflow pattern and is being handled separately (see the #36807 discussion).

Hi all — a short, concrete request rather than a bump.

I've been contributing to `vllm-project/speculators` (see
[vllm-project/speculators#1104](https://github.com/vllm-project/speculators/pull/1104),
merged 2026-09-09) and have a handful of open PRs here that are all sitting behind the
`run-ci` label gate — every test job shows `skipping`, so none of them has ever executed
a single test. Five of them need nothing from me but the label:

**Could you add `run-ci` to these?** (one line each so you can triage in a few minutes)

| PR | what it fixes | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| [#38144](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38144) | JIT `fast_topk` silently truncates when the coarse fp16 threshold bin overflows the 4096-entry smem staging buffer — a **live correctness bug** in `radix_select_topk`. Fix = exact fallback. | On 8×A800: unpatched reproduces **8 failed / 25 passed**; patched **33 passed / 0 failed**; non-overflow path unchanged. Regression test is in the PR. Lint is now green (clang-format fix pushed). |
| [#40362](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40362) | GDN gating beta loses precision on the extend/prefill path; keeps it fp32. | Regression test added and moved into the registered unit taxonomy. Lint is now green (isort + ruff-format fix pushed). |
| [#37061](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37061) | `arg_groups` silently accepts `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` together with NGRAM, which is not a supported combination. Fix = reject at argument resolution instead of failing later. | 3 files, +93/−3. |
| [#38642](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38642) | DFLASH: capture Qwen4-Exp hidden states through the model's own learned HC gate, instead of an uncontracted residual. Without it the aux features the draft consumes do not match what the engine serves. | Branch rebased onto current `main` and pushed; `check-changes` should now be green. |
| [#39391](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39391) | Spec: a draft config that fails to parse currently aborts algorithm resolution; tolerate it and fall back. | 2 files, +86/−9. |

I verified #38144 and #40362 on my own 8×A800 box — that's my measurement, not something
the PR bodies claim, so treat it as a data point rather than upstream evidence.

No other ask — happy to adjust any of these to whatever the project prefers.

@BBuf — gentle ping as the kernel-area Merge Oncall. #38144 (fast_topk staging-overflow fix, 2 files +173/−10) has been locally verified on A800 hardware with a regression matrix (33 cases: unpatched 8 failed / 25 passed → patched 33 passed / 0 failed) — branch tip `e9ba4f06`, rebased on main as of 09-27. It’s currently waiting on the `run-ci` label — could you tag it (plus `run-ci-extra` for the extra suite) when you have a moment? Happy to run any additional checks you need.

**GB10 (DGX Spark, SM121) verification of #38144: the k=512 overflow is real on a real Flash-Next workload, and the patch removes it.**

Independent verification from a different architecture, in case it helps: the PR has SM80 (A800) evidence from the author, this is SM121 (GB10) from someone unrelated to the PR.

**Setup.** DGX Spark (GB10, SM121), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (senfu NVFP4), SGLang fork `4fb9b5b5ba` (2026-09-17) with only the kernel hunk of #38144 applied to `python/sglang/kernels/jit/csrc/elementwise/fast_topk.cuh`. The file in our fork matched the PR's base blob (`b30f4636c819`) and the patched file is blob-identical to the PR head (`851244a87954`). QSA indexer, `kTopK=512` (`indexer_budget 2048 / compress_ratio 4`), chunked prefill 1024, one request at a time. #37893 was not applied (it touches the AOT `topk.cu` and `kpool_topk_transform.cuh`, not this file).

**1. Regression conditions** (standalone port of the PR's test, no pytest; value-multiset comparison against `torch.topk`, same semantics as `_check_topk_values`). 23 cases: concentrated `10.0 + 0.1*N(0,1)` at L=30,938 / 65,504 for k=512 and 2048, 5-run stability, N(0,1) controls, plus decode-shaped `uniform(1.0,1.2)` (B=1/2, L=8,000–95,000), mixed `row_starts`/lengths, and short/boundary rows (L=84…2048).

- Unpatched: **17 of 23 fail** (all concentrated cases, all stability cases, all decode-shaped uniform cases, the row_starts case); controls and short rows pass.
- Patched: **0 of 23 fail.**

**2. Real indexer scores before/after** (observation-only wrapper around `fast_topk`, returning the kernel's own output unchanged; sampled rows compared with `torch.topk`; "wrong" = selected entry strictly below the true k-th value). Inputs: real source-code prompts of 20K–380K tokens (L = compressed blocks = tokens/4, up to ~95K).

- Unpatched (66,537 sampled rows): 0 wrong rows for L ≤ 16K blocks (~22,000 rows); for L > 32K blocks, **prefill 84 / 12,112 rows (0.7%) and decode 114 / 19,569 rows (0.6%)**, up to 84 of 512 entries wrong in a row; threshold bin up to 7,307 entries (> 4096). In a second run that also recorded ranks (26 wrong rows) the best missed rank was 297 at minimum, 443 median, none within the top 256.
- Patched (28,230 sampled rows, 25,254 with L > 16K blocks): **0 wrong rows**, 0 hook errors. 146 rows had a threshold bin above 4096 (max 7,244) — the kind that is wrong without the patch — and all were selected exactly. At the unpatched rate (0.31%) about 86 wrong rows would have been expected.
- Needle retrieval in the final answer at 100K / 150K / 256K / 380K tokens: 1/1, 1/1, 2/2, 3/3 (patched). I did not find an output difference attributable to the missed entries before the patch either (needle retrieval was also correct unpatched), so I cannot claim a visible quality effect — only that the selection is now exact.

**3. CUDA graph.** The wrapper cannot observe graph-replayed decode, so I tested the patched kernel separately: capture once, then replay with changed buffer contents and lengths (B=1/2, overflowing and non-overflowing rows, 18 rows): 0 inexact rows. The server also ran with CUDA graphs enabled in production for 256K/380K needle requests without errors.

**4. Speed.**

- Kernel micro-benchmark (medians, patched → unpatched → patched, same script): non-overflow shapes within noise (e.g. B=1 L=36,000: 18.5 µs both; B=1024 L=32,000: 637–644 µs vs 644 µs); an overflowing row (L=65,504, concentrated) goes 31.9 → 108.7 µs (the exact fallback), which is the cost of being correct.
- End to end (same scripts, unpatched vs patched server): 14-turn growing conversation (70K) 117.9 s vs 114.4 s; prefill-only 93K: 53.9 s vs 54.5 s (3 runs within 0.2%), 260K: 170.2 s vs 170–172 s, 379K: 269.9 s vs 271–273 s (≈ +1%, 1–3 runs per condition). One slower patched measurement right after server start (the first long prompts after startup were ~20–28% slower) was also seen on the unpatched server and disappears on repeat, so I attribute it to start-up, not to the patch.

**Not covered:** the AOT `topk.cu`, k=2048 on a real model path (QSA uses 512; k=2048 only in the synthetic regression cases), content other than concatenated Python source, and the observation wrapper sampled rows (≤ 8 per call; 1 in 8 prefill calls, 1 in 4 decode calls).

For what it is worth, this reproduced and fixed a real failure on hardware the author does not have, so the fix does not look SM80-specific. The kernel blob I tested (`851244a879`) is still the current head here, so these numbers apply to the branch as it stands.

Adding coverage on three more architectures, alongside the SM80 and SM121 results in the thread. We used this PR's head (`e9ba4f0699`) merged onto main `8d4e1ce4c7` (no conflicts) and image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261103-797af717`. We ran `test_fast_topk_regression.py`, then ran the same file again with only `fast_topk.cuh` swapped back to main's version (separate JIT cache):

| GPU | this PR | main `fast_topk.cuh` |
|---|---|---|
| H100 80GB (SM90) | 10 passed | 8 failed, 2 passed |
| RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120) | 10 passed | 8 failed, 2 passed |
| GB200 (SM100) | 10 passed | 8 failed, 2 passed |

The existing `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_fast_topk.py` also passes with this PR on GB200 (23 passed).

On main, all eight overflow cases fail (`threshold_bin_overflow` and `overflow_stable_across_runs` at L = 30,938 / 65,504 × k = 512 / 2048). Only the two non-overflow controls pass, the same split you saw on A800.

We measured a similar change in a downstream build: the stock kernel picked wrong sets on 16 of 16 overflow rows, and the fallback rows cost roughly 12→19 µs, 23→66 µs and 35→120 µs at 8K, 32K and 65K. That is only on rows that actually overflow; other rows are unchanged.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,95 @@
+"""Regression tests for sgl-project/sglang#36807 (JIT fast_topk overflow).
+
+A concentrated row (e.g. 10.0 + 0.1*N(0,1)) puts ~16-34K candidates into the
+coarse fp16 threshold bin, far past the 4096-entry smem staging buffer. The
+buggy kernel silently drops the overflow (plus its fused histogram counts) and
+still returns exactly-k in-range, non-duplicate indices — wrong and unstable.
+
+Place in test/registered/kernels/ops/elementwise/ alongside test_fast_topk.py
+(same _check_topk_values semantics), or run standalone with:
+    PYTHONPATH=<sglang-src>/python pytest test_fast_topk_regression.py
+
+Before the fix these tests FAIL (wrong rows / unstable selections); after the
+exact-fallback fix they PASS.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fast_topk import fast_topk
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=30, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")
+
+
+def _check_topk_values(score, lengths, indices, topk, row_starts):
+    """Selected indices must pick exactly the top-k value multiset.
+
+    Order is unspecified and tie-breaking may differ from torch.topk, so we
+    compare sorted score values, not index sets. Mirrors test_fast_topk.py.
+    """
+    for b in range(score.shape[0]):
+        start = int(row_starts[b]) if row_starts is not None else 0
+        length = int(lengths[b])
+        section = score[b, start : start + length]
+        row = indices[b]
+        if length <= topk:
+            assert torch.equal(
+                row[:length].cpu(), torch.arange(length, dtype=torch.int32)
+            )
+            assert (row[length:] == -1).all()
+            continue
+        assert (row >= 0).all(), "long rows must fill every slot"
+        picked = section[row.long()]
+        expected = torch.topk(section, topk).values
+        assert torch.equal(
+            picked.sort(descending=True).values, expected.sort(descending=True).values
+        ), f"row {b}: top-{topk} value multiset mismatch"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("topk", [512, 2048])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("length", [30938, 65504])
+def test_fast_topk_threshold_bin_overflow(topk, length):
+    # Regression for sgl-project/sglang#36807 (mochgolf): concentrated scores
+    # overflow the 4096-entry staging buffer; selection must stay exact.
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    batch = 4
+    score = 10.0 + 0.1 * torch.randn(batch, length, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+    lengths = torch.full((batch,), length, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    indices = fast_topk(score, lengths, topk)
+    _check_topk_values(score, lengths, indices, topk, None)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("topk", [512, 2048])
+def test_fast_topk_non_overflow_control(topk):
+    # N(0,1) rows at the same length never overflow: selection stays exact.
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    batch, length = 4, 65504
+    score = torch.randn(batch, length, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+    lengths = torch.full((batch,), length, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    indices = fast_topk(score, lengths, topk)
+    _check_topk_values(score, lengths, indices, topk, None)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("topk", [512, 2048])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("length", [30938, 65504])
+def test_fast_topk_overflow_stable_across_runs(topk, length):
+    # The overflow used to be unstable (which candidates survive depends on
+    # atomic arrival order). The fixed kernel must pick the same set every run.
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    batch = 4
+    score = 10.0 + 0.1 * torch.randn(batch, length, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
+    lengths = torch.full((batch,), length, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    first = (
+        score.gather(1, fast_topk(score, lengths, topk).long())
+        .sort(dim=1, descending=True)
+        .values
+    )
+    for _ in range(5):
+        got = (
+            score.gather(1, fast_topk(score, lengths, topk).long())
+            .sort(dim=1, descending=True)
+            .values
+        )
+        assert torch.equal(got, first), "top-k selection unstable across runs"

**2. Real indexer scores before/after** (observation-only wrapper around `fast_topk`, returning the kernel's own output unchanged; sampled rows compared with `torch.topk`; "wrong" = selected entry strictly below the true k-th value). Inputs: real source-code prompts of 20K–380K tokens (L = compressed blocks = tokens/4, up to ~95K).

- Unpatched (66,537 sampled rows): 0 wrong rows for L ≤ 16K blocks (~22,000 rows); for L > 32K blocks, **prefill 84 / 12,112 rows (0.7%) and decode 114 / 19,569 rows (0.6%)**, up to 84 of 512 entries wrong in a row; threshold bin up to 7,307 entries (> 4096). In a second run that also recorded ranks (26 wrong rows) the best missed rank was 297 at minimum, 443 median, none within the top 256.
- Patched (28,230 sampled rows, 25,254 with L > 16K blocks): **0 wrong rows**, 0 hook errors. 146 rows had a threshold bin above 4096 (max 7,244) — the kind that is wrong without the patch — and all were selected exactly. At the unpatched rate (0.31%) about 86 wrong rows would have been expected.
- Needle retrieval in the final answer at 100K / 150K / 256K / 380K tokens: 1/1, 1/1, 2/2, 3/3 (patched). I did not find an output difference attributable to the missed entries before the patch either (needle retrieval was also correct unpatched), so I cannot claim a visible quality effect — only that the selection is now exact.

**3. CUDA graph.** The wrapper cannot observe graph-replayed decode, so I tested the patched kernel separately: capture once, then replay with changed buffer contents and lengths (B=1/2, overflowing and non-overflowing rows, 18 rows): 0 inexact rows. The server also ran with CUDA graphs enabled in production for 256K/380K needle requests without errors.

**4. Speed.**

- Kernel micro-benchmark (medians, patched → unpatched → patched, same script): non-overflow shapes within noise (e.g. B=1 L=36,000: 18.5 µs both; B=1024 L=32,000: 637–644 µs vs 644 µs); an overflowing row (L=65,504, concentrated) goes 31.9 → 108.7 µs (the exact fallback), which is the cost of being correct.
- End to end (same scripts, unpatched vs patched server): 14-turn growing conversation (70K) 117.9 s vs 114.4 s; prefill-only 93K: 53.9 s vs 54.5 s (3 runs within 0.2%), 260K: 170.2 s vs 170–172 s, 379K: 269.9 s vs 271–273 s (≈ +1%, 1–3 runs per condition). One slower patched measurement right after server start (the first long prompts after startup were ~20–28% slower) was also seen on the unpatched server and disappears on repeat, so I attribute it to start-up, not to the patch.

**Not covered:** the AOT `topk.cu`, k=2048 on a real model path (QSA uses 512; k=2048 only in the synthetic regression cases), content other than concatenated Python source, and the observation wrapper sampled rows (≤ 8 per call; 1 in 8 prefill calls, 1 in 4 decode calls).

For what it is worth, this reproduced and fixed a real failure on hardware the author does not have, so the fix does not look SM80-specific. The kernel blob I tested (`851244a879`) is still the current head here, so these numbers apply to the branch as it stands.
